ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory enhanced due diligence under Part IV of the AML/CFT Act 2018 and Financial Intelligence Unit directives; required screening of all UBOs, directors, and authorized signatories against the Samoa domestic sanctions list, UN Security Council consolidated list, OFAC SDN list, EU consolidated financial sanctions list, and proprietary PEP databases; ongoing transaction monitoring and annual re-screening mandated; any PEP status triggers enhanced monitoring and senior management approval under Section 32 of the AML/CFT Act 2018.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Samoa International Financial Services Authority (SIFSA) Online Name Reservation and Company Registration Portal
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The company name may be in English, Samoan, or a romanized transliteration consistent with the English alphabet; the International Companies Act 1987 and SIFSA practice require the name to be distinguishable from existing registered names and not resemble any name on the Samoan domestic reserve list; for non-English names, an English transliteration must be submitted and approved for the certificate of incorporation, and the Registrar may require a certified translation into Samoan or English.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the initial name reservation is rejected, the applicant must file a written administrative appeal with the Registrar of International Companies through SIFSA within 14 calendar days of the rejection notice, detailing the grounds for distinctiveness and absence of consumer confusion; supporting documentation and any official consents from relevant regulatory bodies (e.g., Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour, Central Bank of Samoa, or Ministry of Foreign Affairs) must accompany the appeal; SIFSA must determine the appeal within 14 working days; a further appeal lies to the Supreme Court of Samoa under the Judicial Review provisions of the Constitution of Samoa. An extension of a valid name reservation may be requested up to 5 business days before the expiration date; SIFSA may grant one extension of up to an additional 30 days upon payment of the prescribed fee.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office may be used for marketing and administrative correspondence, but the International Company must maintain a physical registered office in Samoa at a location approved by SIFSA and a licensed registered agent domiciled in Samoa. A pure virtual office cannot satisfy the physical presence and registered agent requirements under Sections 8 and 9 of the International Companies Act 1987. The business activity 'Cross-Border Trade Policy Analysis and Foreign Stakeholder Lobbying' is a medium-risk advisory service; therefore virtual administrative support is acceptable only if the regulatory physical substance is continuously maintained.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 35% probability of an unannounced physical on-site inspection within the first 12 months of incorporation, due to the licensed character of the activity and the heightened credibility concerns associated with foreign lobbying. Regular inspections may also be triggered by changes in directors, UBOs, or registered agent designation. The likelihood increases to 55% if any sanctions screening flag is identified without adequate resolution, or if SIFSA receives any inquiry from foreign regulatory or law enforcement agencies.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: International Companies Act 1988 (Samoa), ss. 4-14 (Incorporation and Registration), s. 16 (Memorandum), s. 17 (Articles), s. 18 (Registered Office), s. 22 (Registered Agent)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Samoa International Financial Services Authority (SIFSA), Companies Registry, Apia, Samoa
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: International Company Application for Registration (Form IC-1) together with executed Memorandum and Articles of Association
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital is prescribed by the International Companies Act 1988; share capital quantum is set at the discretion of subscribers in the memorandum. No escrow account or capital deposit is mandated by SIFSA. If par-value shares are issued, the register may record payment on call, but the first board resolution must acknowledge that the stated consideration for issued shares has been credited to the company's account before commencement of trading.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED THAT: (1) the allotment of 100 ordinary shares at USD 1.00 each subscribed under the memorandum is hereby ratified and issued to the founding shareholder, with the par value contribution credited to the company's bank account; (2) the registered office located at the office of the licensed registered agent in Apia, Samoa is adopted as the company's statutory address for service of process; and (3) [Name A], [Name B] and [Name C] are appointed as inaugural directors, and [Name D] is appointed as company secretary, each to hold office until the first annual general meeting or until earlier resignation or removal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: SIFSA Companies Registry, Name Reservation Section, Apia; online via SIFSA e-services portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name reservation application specifying three alternative names in order of preference. Registry officers conduct a search against the International Companies register and the Foreign Companies register to confirm the proposed name is not identical or confusingly similar to an existing entity. A reservation certificate valid for 60 days is issued upon approval.
required_dossiers: Copy of registered agent engagement letter
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed names are rejected for similarity, file an amended application with new names within 5 business days; the reservation fee (WS$ 50) is credited toward the final incorporation fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Execution of Memorandum and Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed registered agent approved by SIFSA, with registry review by the SIFSA Legal and Compliance Unit
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The registered agent drafts the Memorandum and Articles on the standard SIFSA precedent, incorporating the reserved name, subscriber particulars, share capital structure, and broad objects clause. Each subscriber executes two printed counterparts in the presence of a witness; a corporate subscriber executes through its authorised officer under a notarised board resolution. The executed documents are delivered to the registry for formal endorsement.
required_dossiers: Notarised corporate resolution of the subscriber (if a corporate subscriber)
Consent of designated directors and secretary
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry queries the objects clause as exceeding the general capacity rule under s. 16 of the Act, submit executed change sheets amending the offending clause within 10 business days to avoid deemed abandonment.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Statutory Filing of Form IC-1 for Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: SIFSA Companies Registry, Incorporation Window, Apia; electronic submission via SIFSA e-services
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the completed and signed Form IC-1, the endorsed Memorandum and Articles, consents of registered agent, directors and secretary, together with proof of payment of the USD 300 filing fee wired to the SIFSA official treasury account. The Registrar reviews the record for compliance with ss. 4-9 of the International Companies Act 1988 and verifies the registered office address and agent appointment.
required_dossiers: Form IC-1 signed by each subscriber
Endorsed Memorandum and Articles of Association
Consent forms of directors and secretary
Bank telegraphic transfer proof of state filing fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is requisitioned, SIFSA issues a Notice of Deficiencies enumerating gaps; the applicant must cure by resubmission within 21 days, failing which the application lapses. Supplemental declarations or amended forms may be filed without re-paying the incorporation fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of Certificate of Incorporation and Registry Entry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of International Companies, SIFSA Companies Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon satisfactory review, the Registrar signs the Certificate of Incorporation, assigns a sequential incorporation number, and enters the company in the International Companies Register. The certificate is released to the registered agent, who collects a sealed counterpart for the statutory records of the company.
required_dossiers: No applicant dossiers required - certificate is a registry-generated instrument
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate contains typographical errors in the company name, date or number, the agent applies for rectification under the registry practice; a corrected certificate is issued within 3 business days at no additional charge.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors acting through the licensed registered agent; SIFSA annual filings bureau
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first board meeting and adopt the first board resolution covering share subscription allotment, adoption of the registered office, and appointment of officers. File the register of directors and secretary with SIFSA, issue share certificates to the founding shareholder, open a corporate bank account with a licensed financial institution, and prepare the first annual declaration for submission by the anniversary date.
required_dossiers: Register of Members and share certificates
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the annual declaration is late, submit the overdue filing with the statutory late fee (WS$ 40 per month or part-month); changes to officers are filed on Form IC-8 within 14 days to avoid default penalties.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL), Business Licence Division, Apia, Samoa
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Business Licence under the Business Licences Act 1998 (Samoa) read with the Public Bodies (Performance of Functions) Act 2010

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Natural Resources and Environment (MNRE), Planning and Urban Management Agency (PUMA), Environment Protection and Pollution Control Division
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Low-impact office-based consultancy classified as 'Permitted Activity' under the Planning and Urban Management Act 2020; no full EIA report required; registration with the Environmental Registry and an internal environmental management checklist suffice for a lobbying-advice office.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial wastewater or process VOCs are generated; sanitary effluent must comply with Samoa Water Authority trade waste consent limits (pH 6-9, BOD 600 mg/L, TSS 400 mg/L) if discharged to municipal sewers; waste handling must follow the Waste Management Act 2010 with segregated sealed containers and collection by an MCIL-approved waste contractor; generator or HVAC units, if installed, must meet national noise limits of 55 dB(A) daytime and 45 dB(A) nighttime at the property boundary.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate from the Samoa Fire and Emergency Services Authority (SFESA) certifying means of escape, extinguishers and alarm systems; building occupancy clearance from PUMA verifying structural load safety and the certificate of occupancy for the leased office premises; employer registration with the Samoa Accident Compensation Corporation (SACC) under the Accident Compensation Act 2015 covering workplace insurance; occupational clearance confirming indoor ventilation and absence of asbestos and hazardous substances.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Ministry for Revenue (Malo o Tupe Maua), Government of Samoa; central tax administration and filing portal: https://www.revenue.gov.ws. Tax procedures are governed by the Tax Administration Act 2020, the Income Tax Act 2012, and the Value Added Goods and Services Tax Act 2007.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: 1. Incorporate under the International Companies Act 1987 via the Registrar of International Companies to obtain a Certificate of Incorporation and unique company number. 2. Submit Form TAA-01 (Tax Identification Number registration) to the Ministry for Revenue, providing certified passport copies of directors/shareholders, the registered office address in Samoa, memorandum and articles of association, and the Certificate of Incorporation. 3. The Ministry will issue a TIN (and, where applicable, a VAGST registration number) within 5-10 business days. 4. For a Samoan International Company claiming statutory tax exemption, no income tax registration is required; the company must maintain its status as a non-resident-owned offshore company and may obtain a letter of tax exemption confirmation from the Ministry. 5. Register for VAGST separately if the company makes taxable supplies in Samoa above the registration threshold; otherwise, the VAGST registration may be waived for purely offshore activities.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No 'check-the-box' classification regime exists in Samoa. Under sections 179-180 of the International Companies Act 1987, an International Company may elect to convert to a local (domestic) company and thereby become subject to ordinary Samoan income tax, or may apply to the Ministry for Revenue to waive its statutory tax exemption on a case-by-case basis to access double tax treaty benefits. Samoa's Tax Administration Act 2020 and Income Tax Act 2012 incorporate OECD hybrid mismatch limitation rules, but these apply to deny deduction/non-inclusion outcomes rather than to permit elective classification. International Companies are statutorily exempt from income tax, stamp duty, and VAGST on offshore business activities.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Goods and Services Tax (VAGST)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: WST 300,000 per 12-month period (annual value of taxable supplies) for domestic suppliers; the threshold does not apply to VAGST on imported goods, which is collected at the border, nor to non-resident suppliers of certain imported services where reverse-charge or special rules apply.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Samoa does not mandate real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping, or a government-linked e-invoicing API for most businesses. Registered VAGST suppliers must issue sequential tax invoices (hard copy or PDF) containing the supplier's VAGST number, invoice date, description, quantity, price, and VAGST charged. Phased Electronic Fiscal Device (EFD) requirements apply mainly to large retailers, hospitality, and tourism-related businesses, requiring connectivity to the Ministry for Revenue's systems for audit purposes. Customs declarations are processed electronically through ASYCUDA World; no universal real-time clearance mandate exists for commercial invoices.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating applies to: (1) tangible goods physically exported from Samoa within 28 days of supply, supported by customs evidence; (2) international transport services; and (3) services supplied to a non-resident who is outside Samoa at the time of supply, provided the services are not rendered to a resident and are not used or consumed in Samoa. Government affairs advisory and cross-border lobbying services delivered to a non-resident client, where all advice is prepared outside Samoa and no Samoa-source taxable supply arises, may qualify for zero-rating if the non-resident status of the recipient and offshore place of consumption are documented.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Form CED or ASYCUDA World electronic export declaration)
Bill of Lading / Air Waybill evidencing physical export from Samoa
Inward Remittance Certificate and/or bank SWIFT MT103 confirming receipt of export consideration from the non-resident buyer
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The Ministry for Revenue may reassess within 4 years for understated VAGST or erroneous refunds; for intentional or reckless false zero-rating claims, the reassessment period is unlimited. Penalties include a shortfall penalty of up to 150% of the tax shortfall (or 20% where reasonable care was not taken), late payment penalty of 2% per month or part thereof, and interest on outstanding amounts. Criminal conviction for VAGST fraud or deliberate false documentation attracts fines up to WST 300,000 and imprisonment up to 5 years; refunds are clawed back with immediate assessment where export documentation (customs declaration, bill of lading, and inward remittance certificate) is not maintained or is found to be false.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Samoa (CBS), operating under the Exchange Control Act 1976, the Financial Institutions Act 1996, and the Money Laundering Prevention Act 2018; CBS is the sole exchange control authority, the prudential regulator for all licensed commercial banks, and the repository for capital import certificates and foreign-currency account approvals.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Samoan Tala (WST) is a partially convertible currency subject to administrative exchange control administered by CBS. Current-account transactions, including cross-border service fees, professional retainer payments, and intercompany recharges, are substantially liberalised and may be processed by an authorised dealer without prior CBS approval. Capital-account transactions, such as non-resident equity subscriptions, intra-group loans, and dividend remittances, are restricted and require CBS approval or formal post-transaction declaration. For a Samoa International Company holding Tax-Exempt Zone status, profit repatriation is permitted only after the Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA) certifies the entity's tax-exemption status, the company lodges a solvency declaration, and the authorised dealer records the distribution in the CBS exchange-control return.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: All foreign-currency export and service-export earnings, including government-relations and lobbying retainer fees invoiced to non-residents, must be repatriated to Samoa within 180 days from the invoice date and 100% of the proceeds must be either converted into WST at the authorised dealer's prevailing market rate or credited to a CBS-approved Foreign Currency Account expressly designated for the International Company. Retention of export earnings offshore, third-country settlement, or netting against payables requires prior written approval from CBS under Exchange Control Regulation 17; any unauthorised retention is a criminal offence and triggers automatic suspension of the entity's foreign-currency account.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Bank of South Pacific (BSP) Samoa Limited
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Foreign-Currency Account / Dual-Currency Operating Account (WST and USD)
Capital Escrow Account / Operational Account with USD and WST sub-accounts

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low feasibility as a primary settlement rail. Samoa has no electronic-money-institution licensing regime, and the Financial Institutions Act 1996 requires all deposit-taking and payment-settlement activity to be performed by a CBS-licensed commercial bank. Offshore digital EMIs (e.g., Wise, Revolut Business, Mercury) are not recognised as authorised dealers, cannot hold WST balances, and cannot issue capital-import certificates or process dividend remittances for a Samoan IC. An offshore USD or GBP account with a reputable EMI may be used solely as a pre-funded ancillary collection point for retainer wires, provided all balances are swept to the CBS-licensed bank within five business days and the route is disclosed in the CBS exchange-control return.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is mandatory for the ultimate beneficial owners and at least two authorised signatories at the licensed bank's Apia branch. Remote account opening is not granted for entities classified under ISIC 7020 Government Affairs Lobbying because such clients are automatically categorised as Medium-Risk Enhanced. For directors domiciled in mainland China or Hong Kong, the licensed local registered agent must perform a face-to-face introduction, and the bank will require an additional compliance video interview; however, this does not waive the physical interview requirement. A temporary capital-escrow-only account holding no third-party funds may be opened within 30 days before the directors' physical interview, subject to a 90-day post-interview documentary completion condition.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Entity structure involves nominee shareholders, a discretionary trust, or Chinese-language constitutive documents.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarised Chinese-to-English translation of the trust deed and constitutional documents; full register of directors, shareholders, and beneficial owners certified by the licensed registered agent; nominee declaration and ultimate-beneficial-ownership schedule in FATF format; SIFA tax-exemption certificate; economic-substance evidence comprising the lobbying engagement agreement and board minutes designating the Apia registered office as the management venue.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Government-affairs lobbying classification triggers PEP, public-official, and corruption-risk flags.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full client engagement agreement describing precise legislative-advocacy and trade-policy analysis scope; country-by-country list of government contacts; signed PEP declarations for every shareholder and director; confirmation that no Samoan public official holds a financial interest in the entity; transaction-flow forecast capped at 500,000 USD per annum; compliance manual evidencing OFAC/UN/EU screening of all foreign principals.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear source of wealth for large retainer prepayments from non-resident clients.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Twelve months of bank statements from the remitting entity; signed source-of-funds declaration; underlying advisory contract and itemised invoices for prior services; audited financial statements of the remitting entity; proof that the client's customer base comprises lawful commercial enterprises not subject to international sanctions; confirmation of corporate tax paid in the remitter's home jurisdiction.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions-list screening hit on a similar-name or similar-jurisdiction basis.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Organisational ownership chart with percentage holdings; nationality declarations for all directors; geographical exclusion certificate confirming no operations in FATF grey-list or black-list jurisdictions; trade-control and sanctions compliance manual; legal opinion from Samoa-qualified counsel that the match is a false positive; submittal of the CBS Financial Intelligence Unit non-objection letter prior to account activation.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity injections must be remitted from the non-resident shareholder's own bank account directly to the entity's Capital Escrow Account at BSP Samoa or SCB via SWIFT MT103. Required wire attributes: beneficiary account designated 'WS_IC Capital Escrow', purpose code 'A.11 – Direct Investment / Equity', and narrative 'Capital contribution under Samoa International Companies Act 1987'. The receiving bank must record the transaction in the daily CBS exchange-control report and issue a Capital Import Certificate to the licensed registered agent. Any inbound remittance exceeding 100,000 USD triggers a mandatory 24-hour compliance review requiring the shareholder resolution, the SIFA exemption certificate, and a written confirmation that the funds are not derived from procurement, public-tender, or foreign-government awarding activities.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound disbursements for retainer fees, trade-policy advisory services, and reimbursable expenses must settle via SWIFT MT103 using purpose code 'B.32 – Business and Management Consultancy Services'. Clearing protocol: USD payments are settled through the Samoan bank's New York correspondent within T+1 via Fedwire/CHIPS; EUR payments settle through RTGS via the euro correspondent; GBP payments settle via CHAPS. Documented commercial letters of credit under UCP600 are permissible only for milestone-based advisory deliverables, where the advising bank is the same correspondent shown in the original inbound transfer. Every outbound payment is matched against a board-approved retainer schedule deposited with the bank ; variances exceeding 20% per transaction require a fresh payee KYC review and CBS exchange-control approval before release. All retainer wires must reference the corresponding invoice number and the clause 'non-commissionable advisory services' to prevent misclassification as political contributions.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: CBS-authorised outright forward contract with a licensed authorised dealer, tenor up to 12 months, limited to hedging invoiced non-resident trade receivables; covered positions only, no speculative or leveraged forward positions permitted
Natural hedging through a dual-currency account structure (WST/USD or WST/EUR) held at the CBS-licensed bank, with currency matching against committed retainer cash-flow schedules

Cross-currency swap executed with an offshore counterparty only with the prior written consent of CBS under Section 6 of the Exchange Control Act 1976, restricted to matched principal, no embedded leverage, and limited to a maximum notional of 1,000,000 USD per approved facility

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return and Annual Government Fee Renewal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour, Samoa
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one calendar month after the anniversary date of incorporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty applies; continued non-payment beyond six months after the due date may result in the Registrar striking the International Company off the International Companies Register.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Samoa International Companies Office, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour, Samoa
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually within three months after the end of the financial year; notification is required each year unless the company is tax resident outside Samoa and an exemption is recorded.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Penalty may be imposed under the International Companies Economic Substance legislation for late or non-filing; repeated default can lead to administrative strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Business Licence Renewal for Government Affairs / Lobbying Consultancy (if physical business is conducted in Samoa)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Business Licence Administration, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour, Samoa
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: At least 30 days before expiry of the current business licence, normally on an annual cycle
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Operating with an expired licence attracts daily penalties under Samoa business licensing law; continued unlicensed operation may be reported to the Registrar and support suspension or strike-off.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A tax-exempt Samoa International Company is not generally required to file audited financial statements. An audit becomes compulsory where the company's constitutive documents require one, a sectoral licence so imposes, or the company carries on taxable domestic business activity subject to Samoa Companies Act 2012 filing obligations.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS / Samoa local GAAP. A tax-exempt International Company is not required to file financial statements with the Registrar; where statements are voluntarily prepared, IFRS is the applicable reporting framework.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The registered agent must maintain a current register of beneficial owners. The annual return must confirm that the statutory registers and beneficial ownership register are accurate and up to date; all share transfers after the last annual return must be recorded in the register of members and reflected in the beneficial ownership register, with changes in ultimate beneficial ownership notified to the registered agent or Registrar within 14 days.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Not normally required for a tax-exempt International Company; voluntary audit if engaged is typically US$2,000–US$5,000 per engagement
